_about: Every digit run in this file is a published test card number (4111111111111111, 378282246310005, 4222222222222, 5500000000000004, 4012888888881881, 5555555555554444, 2223000048400011, 6011111111111117, 3530111333300000, 36227206271667, 3056930009020004, 6200000000000005, 6205500000000000004, 6304000000000000, 5063516945005047) or a number generated here to pass or fail the Luhn check; a generated card number is a published one with its prefix swapped and its check digit recomputed. No real card number is in this file.
_rule: A run is the longest digit sequence with at most 3 separator characters in a row between digits; a group is a maximal sequence of digits inside a run, with no separator in it. A run is refused when its whole digit string has 13 to 19 digits and passes the Luhn check (the original rule, whatever the digits are), or when a span of whole consecutive groups of it has 13 to 19 digits, passes Luhn, is a brand's number (its leading digits fall in an issuer prefix of one row of the brand table and its length is one that same row uses) and has an accepted layout: a card's layout (one group; or every group 4 digits but the last, which holds 1 to 4; or 4-6-5; or 4-6-4) or a card's layout of the same total with one slip (one group split in two, two neighbouring groups joined, or the boundary of two neighbouring groups moved by one digit); the owner cured the spacing slip on 2026-11-19, and the accepted layouts are listed under layout_vectors. A group of more than 19 digits is never part of a span. The owner narrowed the strict rule on 2026-11-19 because it refused honest notes of bare numbers set side by side. Every character with the Unicode property White_Space is a separator after normalisation (the owner asked for it on 2026-11-19; the code points are listed under separator_vectors, and the white-* vectors pin it). Text is flattened (paragraphs, list items, quote paragraphs and hard breaks joined by one line feed), normalised NFKC, format characters dropped. Entries marked limit are cases the guard does NOT refuse; each is pinned so that nobody later believes otherwise. Entries with a note say which decision of 2026-11-19 moved them. Expected values were computed with the reference guard of the design, the strict ones by hand and then by an independent brute force, and the narrowed ones by an independent brute force of the narrowed rule with the brand table written as one regular expression per brand, not with the guard under test. The slip vectors (ids slip-* and double-slip-*) take their expected values from the measurer's reference of the picked layout test, not from the guard: a number of every brand with one slip in its spacing is refused, with two slips it is allowed as a stated limit.

separator_vectors._about: The separator characters of the card number guard as code points, after NFKC. Every character with the Unicode property White_Space is a separator (the owner asked for it on 2026-11-19); the hyphen-minus, U+2010 to U+2015 and the minus sign are separators too. code_points is the exact set both guards hold; added_2026_11_19 is the six that were missing; white_space_members is the property's 25 members, each of which is in code_points or is turned into a plain space by NFKC.
